prospective_note: every pull request in this population was merged before the protocol was frozen. This is a shadow over the recent merged traffic of five public repositories the product has never reviewed, not a prospective run, and no claim from it may say otherwise.
population_rule: the first six candidates, in the owner's order, whose free evaluability probe passes (probe.json, run 34659752086; the first dispatch probe-run-1.json failed two on the probe's own stub); five passed, so the population is five
unit: one merged pull request; head = its merge commit (what the target branch became when it landed, a squash and a merge commit alike) and base = that commit's first parent, which is the target branch as it stood the moment before and therefore merge-base(head, target branch at merge time). The diff base..head is exactly what the pull request contributed.
selection: per repository, the four most recently merged pull requests by merged_at descending that changed at least one Python file of the package itself -- a .py file outside tests/, docs/, examples/ and packaging scaffolding -- and whose diff does not exceed 2000 changed lines (additions plus deletions, from the GitHub API's file list). A pull request that fails either rule is recorded in selection.json with its reason and the walk continues. The merge commit must resolve in the read-only clone; one that does not is recorded and skipped.
order: round-robin across repositories in name order, four per repository, newest merged first within a repository, so a cost cap removes units evenly rather than whole repositories
exclusion_declared_before_any_run: none beyond the selection rule. No unit is excluded after its outcome is known, nothing is re-sampled and nothing is retried.
switches: value_notes_visible and gate_notes_visible on for every unit, so every author-visible line is recorded to the lines file; contained_attempt_voids at the product default (D-226); intent_replies off (no GitHub client exists on this path)
smoke: before the twenty are bought, exactly one unit is run under --limit 1 into a separate trials file (trials-smoke.jsonl) with the per-unit budget lowered to $0.30 by --unit-budget, so a $0.30 reservation can start it under the D-172 rule. It is a pipeline check that the artifact carries a ledger and a lines file (AGENTS.md section 9), never a measurement: the same unit is bought again at $1.00 in the main run and only that trial counts.
truth: the owner adjudicates every author-visible line by hand into three columns (useful / true but not actionable / wrong) in the dated report; no line is adjudicated by this study's code
retries: none; a unit that cannot run is recorded with its DEFER or refusal reason
silence_reporting: every silent unit records units_read and units_total; a silence over a partly-read pull request covers only what was read
code: the release/batch2 branch of 2026-09-13, which carries D-232 (attest.intent.v5), D-233 and D-234
freeze_at_note: the host clock, UTC, written by the freeze step immediately before selection
authorization_erratum: 2026-09-12T00:02Z, before any unit ran and with $0.00 spent: authorization.json's granted_at had been written as 2026-09-12T14:00Z, a calendar guess after the host-clock freeze -- the same erratum e05-external-v1 recorded -- and preflight would have refused it. granted_at is corrected to the UTC instant the work order was received, before this window's first commit, and the protocol digest re-frozen; freeze_at, the sample and the order are untouched, and no outcome existed to influence the correction.
